scope: cryptanalysis cb73ed6f; instances generated-16..24bit (registry-fresh seeds) and 24/28/32 bit (registry-ext seeds), one curve per size, 24 planted targets, 10 (16-24 bit) or 6 (24/28/32 bit ext) replicate processes per arm in rotated order pinned to one CPU; raw reports archived in-repo (S3 unavailable); 4 vCPU cloud VM shared with another agent; wall time is this host's
statement: Accounting audit of mitm-prime-batched m=2 (all rows verified [d]G=Q, identical trials and relations to mitm): the registry priced-S ratio vs the registry baseline (4.45 at 24 bits) factors into the negation fold the baseline arm does not use (counted S 1.79x; wall 1.39x), the pricing convention (scalar build charged as counted additions at the calibrated ns/add versus measured ns: 1.75x S, 0 wall) and the genuine batching gain 1.41x S / 1.37x wall [1.36,1.39] against the same-priced folded scalar build mitm:negation_folded=1,native_setup_pricing=1. Genuine wall gain of the lead against that control at m=2: 1.09, 1.20, 1.30, 1.34, 1.37 at 16, 18, 20, 22, 24 bits and 1.41, 1.50, 1.65 at 24, 28, 32 bits; against the registry baseline wall 1.27-1.94x (16-24 bits) and 1.91, 2.38, 2.28 (24, 28, 32 bits). Priced-S ratio vs the registry baseline at 24, 28, 32 bits is 4.77, 5.24, 3.77 (m=3: 4.24, 3.98, 2.60): it peaks near 28 bits and falls, while lead S over the matched rho.negation rises 7.2, 14.9, 26.5.
